title: Federated Telemetry and Cost Aggregation Protocol (FTCAP) — Design Spec
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview

This design spec describes the Federated Telemetry and Cost Aggregation Protocol (FTCAP). FTCAP standardizes how telemetry-producing components across Redwood Inference (hosted, dedicated, private edge, and partner proxies) emit usage and fidelity signals, and how downstream aggregators compute cost-attribution, SLO alignment, and billing-ready metrics. The protocol is intended to be lightweight, extensible, and resilient to partial failure.

Goals

- Provide a single wire format and interaction pattern for usage telemetry and fidelity signals across deployment surfaces (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Private VPC agents, and edge proxies).
- Enable deterministic cost aggregation per-tenant, per-route, and per-model-variant with stable semantics for billing and SLA reconciliations.
- Preserve low-latency path for production inference; telemetry must not add >1% p95 request latency overhead.
- Support batched and streaming modes for different runtime constraints.
- Be auditable and verifiable by both Redwood and enterprise customers (where applicable) to support disputes and compliance.

Non-goals

- FTCAP does not prescribe billing rates or pricing tiers. It provides accounting primitives only.
- FTCAP does not replace full trace/span systems for distributed tracing; it complements them with cost-centric, compact usage payloads.

Background and motivation

Current state: multiple services (runtime workers, local prefetch proxies, hybrid-cache coordinators, and Dedicated control-plane agents) emit telemetry in heterogeneous formats. This makes cross-surface cost aggregation error-prone and costly to reconcile. Discrepancies cause customer confusion and slow incident resolution.

FTCAP addresses:
- Canonicalizing fields for token accounting, embedding units, KV cache reuse credits, batching amortization, and fidelity adjustments.
- Providing signatures and sequence numbers for tamper-evidence and replay protections.
- Defining a reconciliation plan for asynchronous delivery and partial visibility.

High-level architecture

- Producers: inference runtime workers, local prefetch proxies, edge SDKs. They emit FTCAP messages at request end or periodically for batch/stream windows.
- Ingest gateway: lightweight collector that validates schema, enforces landlord quotas, and forwards to Aggregators. Implemented as an autoscaling k8s service in Hosted and as a dockerized collector in Private.
- Aggregators: stateful services that compute per-tenant aggregated metrics and expose queryables and export sinks (billing pipeline, observability pipeline, SLO dashboard).
- Storage: time-series store for near-term SLO/observability (Prometheus/TSDB), and an append-only ledger store for audit and billing (S3-backed Parquet partitions + ledger index).

FTCAP message model (wire format)

- Transport: HTTP/2 POST /ftcap/v1/ingest (primary), gRPC proxy option for low-latency environments, and a batched file upload S3 path for air-gapped on-prem sites.
- Content type: application/json; charset=utf-8

Example message (single-request mode):

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "producer_id": "runtime-worker-42",
  "producer_region": "us-west-2",
  "seq": 45231,
  "timestamp": "2026-09-30T14:22:03.123Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct_12345",
  "route_id": "chat-completion:v2",
  "model_variant": "llama-3-13b-quantized-q4f16",
  "request_id": "req_9a7f3b",
  "tokens": {
    "prompt_tokens": 64,
    "generated_tokens": 128,
    "cached_kv_hits": 12
  },
  "fidelity": {
    "quant_profile": "q4f16",
    "response_fidelity_score": 0.98
  },
  "batching": {
    "batch_size": 4,
    "batch_amortized_credits": 0.25
  },
  "cost_adjustments": {
    "discount_type": "preemptible-credit",
    "units": 0.5
  },
  "signature": "base64sig..."
}

Notes on fields:
- seq: monotonic for a producer instance, used to detect missed/replayed payloads.
- cached_kv_hits: used to reduce billed prompt tokens; aggregator applies the configured cache-credit policy.
- batch_amortized_credits: fraction of baseline per-request token cost charged to this request due to batching.

Batched window mode (when per-request is infeasible):

{
  "version":"1.0",
  "producer_id":"proxy-nyc-08",
  "window_start":"2026-09-30T14:20:00Z",
  "window_end":"2026-09-30T14:20:05Z",
  "tenant_id":"acct_23456",
  "aggregates":{
    "requests": 280,
    "total_prompt_tokens": 10240,
    "total_generated_tokens": 20480,
    "kv_hit_tokens": 5120
  },
  "batching_profile":"adaptive-low-latency",
  "signature":"base64sig..."
}

Cost aggregation rules (summary table)

| Component                | Primary metric                    | Aggregation rule (default)                                  |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Prompt billing          | prompt_tokens - kv_credit         | sum over time windows, apply tenant kv_credit policy        |
| Generation billing      | generated_tokens                  | sum, minus batch amortization credits                       |
| Embedding units         | embedding_units                   | sum, round up to embedding_unit_granularity                 |
| Cache reuse credits     | cached_kv_hits                    | convert to token-equivalent using configured kv_to_token    |
| Batching amortization   | batch_amortized_credits           | distributed evenly across requests in batch                |
| Fidelity adjustments    | response_fidelity_score/flags     | apply fidelity_multiplier table per route/model            |

SLO and billing alignment mapping

- The Aggregator maintains per-route SLO windows and maps observed telemetry to SLO burn and billing credits using deterministic rules.
- Example mapping: if response_fidelity_score < 0.85, mark request as "degraded" and apply fidelity_discount 0.5 to generated token billing until further review.

Deterministic reconciliation

- Each aggregator computes both a nearline and offline view. Nearline view is used for SLO alerts and rough billing; offline ledger view is authoritative for invoicing.
- Producers and collectors keep sequence windows to allow replays. A three-phase reconcile is defined:
  1) Nearline aggregation (minutes latency)
  2) End-of-day ledger rollup (1–3 hours)
  3) Audit pass with producer-signed manifests (up to 24 hours)

Security, signing and tamper evidence

- Every FTCAP message must include a signature header or field. Hosted producers use mTLS + service key signing. Private deployments use customer-provided HSM keys or Redwood-managed delegation keys.
- Sequence numbers and producer monotonic IDs are used to detect gaps. Aggregators record any gaps and mark affected windows for audit.

API contract and validation rules

- Required fields: version, producer_id, tenant_id, timestamp, request_id OR window_start/window_end, tokens or aggregates, signature. Missing required fields -> 400.
- Size cap: single-request message <= 8KB. Batched windows <= 2MB.
- Schema evolution: version field must be present; older versions are accepted with mapping rules in the ingest gateway.

Operational and rollout plan

1. Phase 0 — Pilot (2 weeks): implement ingest gateway in staging; onboard internal runtime workers and Redwood Console; validate parity with current billing pipeline for a narrow set of tenants.
2. Phase 1 — Partner pilot (4 weeks): enable Dedicated collectors in 2 enterprise clients with read-only audit exports; measure divergence vs current instrumentation.
3. Phase 2 — Controlled ramp (6–8 weeks): flip ingestion for 25% of hosted traffic; compare nearline aggregator metrics with legacy sums; adjust kv_to_token and batching profiles.
4. Phase 3 — Full rollout (2–4 weeks): deprecate legacy emitters once reconciliation error < 0.1% for 7 consecutive days.

Migration considerations

- Backwards compatibility: ingest gateway will accept legacy envelopes and translate them to FTCAP.
- Reconciliation window: maintain legacy pipeline in parallel for 90 days after rollout to catch edge cases.

Observability and dashboards

- Aggregators expose these dashboards: per-tenant billing delta, producer gap events, sequence-health heatmap, fidelity-score distributions, and cost-per-model-variant trending.
- Alerts:
  - gap-events.rate > 0.1% sustained -> PagerDuty SEV2 (ownership: infra-observability)
  - daily billing divergence > 0.5% for top 50 tenants -> Billing ops review (ownership: finance-legal + product)

Security and compliance notes

- Sensitive fields (tenant_id, request_id) must be redacted in public exports. Audit exports to customers may include signed manifests and obfuscated request_ids.
- Private deployments must document key rotation procedures and provide HSM integration steps in the onprem packaging docs.

Testing and validation matrix

1) Unit tests: schema validation, signature verification, sequence gap detection.
2) Integration tests: producer -> gateway -> aggregator against reference aggregator in CI.
3) Reconciliation tests: synthetic traffic with known distributions to ensure offline ledger matches expected costs within 0.05%.
4) Chaos tests: simulate dropped messages and replay; verify idempotency and dedupe behavior.

Sample CLI and curl examples

- HTTP ingest (single request):
curl -X POST \"https://ingest.redwood.ai/ftcap/v1/ingest\" \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -H 'X-FTCAP-Signature: base64sig...' \\
  -d '@sample_ftcap_request.json'

- Local batched upload (air-gapped):
aws s3 cp ftcap-window-20260930-1420.json s3://customer-onprem-ftcap/uploads/ --profile onprem-upload

Ownership and next steps

- Spec owner: Priya Menon (eng-product, serving-runtime)
- Implementing teams: eng-serving-runtime (producers), eng-platform (ingest gateway & aggregators), eng-infra (storage & ledger pipeline), finance-legal (billing contract mapping), product (SLO/billing mappings).
- Next steps: formalize fidelity_multiplier table; produce reference SDK for producers (Go + Python); implement ingest gateway rate-limits and schema registry.

Appendix A — Fidelity multiplier example table

| Fidelity band          | response_fidelity_score range | multiplier |
|------------------------|-------------------------------|------------|
| High                   | 0.95 - 1.00                   | 1.00       |
| Standard               | 0.85 - 0.94                   | 0.90       |
| Degraded               | 0.60 - 0.84                   | 0.50       |
| Failed                 | 0.00 - 0.59                   | 0.00       |

Appendix B — Reconciliation SLA expectations

- Nearline accuracy: aggregators should match producer-signed manifests with >= 99.5% token parity within 30 minutes.
- Ledger finalization: end-of-day rollups complete within 3 hours and be ready for billing pipeline ingestion.

Contact and review cadence

- Weekly spec sync: Tuesdays 11:00 PT (owners and reviewers).
- Change control: all breaking schema changes require an ADR and two approvers from eng-platform and finance-legal.
